Minimize the surrogate MI sum $\sum_{i<j} I(\theta_j - \theta_i)$ with respect to $\theta_i \in [0, 2\pi)$ [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the goal is to minimize the entropy of data given projections H(D|X). It derives that this is equivalent to maximizing the joint entropy of projections H(X). Through the decomposition of joint entropy, it shows that H(X) = sum(H(Xi)) - sum(I(Xi; Xj)). Since the marginal entropies H(Xi) are constant with respect to angle selection, maximizing H(X) is equivalent to minimizing the sum of pairwise mutual information terms sum(I(Xi; Xj)). The evidence further specifies that under the stationarity assumption, the pairwise mutual information depends only on the angular separation, i.e., I(Xi; Xj) = I(theta_j - theta_i). Therefore, the claim that one should minimize the surrogate MI sum sum_{i<j} I(theta_j - theta_i) is fully supported by the logical derivation provided in the source text.
supported

It operates on the principle that maximizing the joint entropy of the projections $H(\mathcal{X})$ reduces the uncertainty of the underlying data, which is achieved by minimizing the sum of pairwise mutual information (MI) terms between all projection pairs [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the method aims to minimize the entropy of the data given the projections H(D|X). It derives that H(D|X) = H(D) + H(X|D) - H(X), where H(D) and H(X|D) are independent of the projection angles. Therefore, minimizing H(D|X) is equivalent to maximizing the joint entropy of the projections H(X). The evidence further decomposes H(X) into marginal entropies minus the sum of pairwise mutual information terms (under the assumption that higher-order mutual information is negligible or approximated by pairwise terms). Consequently, maximizing H(X) is achieved by minimizing the sum of pairwise mutual information terms.
